abstract: We report that Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) modulates skeletal muscle function. TLR2 ligands accelerated muscle fatigue development in isolated muscle fibers. Muscle fibers from TLR2 gene knock-out (TLR2-/-) mice were more fatigue resistant. This was not due to altered mitochondrial oxidative capacity or glycogen content. TLR2-/- muscle fibers had larger tetanic [Ca2+]i transients. Muscles from TLR2-/- mice had increased levels of Ca2+-binding proteins compared to WT muscles. Lastly, TLR2 was expressed in muscle fibers of control subjects and patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), whereas high mobility group box protein (HMGB) 1, an endogenous activator of TLR2, was only detected in the cytoplasm of muscles from IIM patients. In conclusion, TLR2 signaling regulates force production in skeletal muscle. TLR2 and its endogenous ligand, HMGB1 likely contribute to the muscle weakness in IIM and, possibly, other muscle disorders. Therapies targeted to the TLR2 signaling pathway may counteract pathological muscle weakness.
